The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

content:
# Slider

Use Slider to choose one number from a continuous range when the approximate value matters more than the exact one.

A track between a minimum and a maximum with a thumb that marks the chosen value. People drag the thumb or step it with the keyboard, and the current value is shown beside the label.

## When to use

- Set a level where people judge by feel and see the effect, such as volume or brightness.
- Narrow a range filter to an approximate amount, such as a maximum price.

## When not to use

- Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Use [Text field](component.text-field) instead. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.
- Choose from a few named options, such as Small, Medium, and Large. Use [Select](component.select) instead. Named options are choices, not points on a scale. A select names each one.
- Show progress or a measured amount people cannot change. Use [Progress bar](component.progress-bar) instead. A slider is a control. A bar that only reports a value must not look adjustable.
- Turn a single setting on or off. Use [Switch](component.switch) instead. Two states are a toggle, not a range.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Header, track, hint, and error stacked together. |
| header | container | Label and value on one line. |
| label | label | Visible name for the value. |
| value | description | The current value as text, at the end of the header. |
| track | container | The line from the minimum to the maximum. |
| fill | indicator | The part of the track from the minimum to the thumb. |
| thumb | interactive-surface | The handle people drag or step to change the value. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| error | string |  |  | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the slider invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| value | number |  |  | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. Defaults to min. |
| min | number |  | `0` | Smallest value, at the start of the track. |
| max | number |  | `100` | Largest value, at the end of the track. Greater than min. |
| step | number |  | `1` | Distance between the values people can choose, counted from min. The value is always min plus a whole number of steps. |
| name | string |  |  | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents changing the value. A disabled slider does not submit its value. |

## Events

- `input`: The value changed while a person drags the thumb or presses a key. Reported for every new value.
- `change`: A person finished changing the value: released the thumb or the key. Reported once, and only when the value differs from the value before they started.

## States

`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `dragging`, `disabled`, `invalid`

## Rules

### Content

- **MUST** visible-label: Provide a visible label that names what the value sets, such as Volume.
- **MUST** value-shown: Show the current value as text beside the label, and give assistive technology the same text. Position on the track alone does not say the value.

### Behavior

- **MUST** value-in-range: The value is always between min and max and lands on a step. A value given outside the range moves to the nearest end, and a value between steps moves to the nearest step.
- **MUST** drag-or-press: Dragging the thumb or pressing anywhere on the track moves the value to that point and reports input for each new value.
- **MUST** keyboard-steps: Arrow keys move the value by one step, Page Up and Page Down by a tenth of the range rounded to a step, and Home and End to min and max. Each key press reports input then change.
- **MUST** change-on-release: Report change once when a person releases the thumb or the key, and only when the value differs from the value before they started. Apply costly work, such as a new search, on change rather than input.
- **MUST** programmatic-no-events: Setting the value from outside, or a form reset, does not report input or change.
- **SHOULD** form-value: Inside a form the value submits under name. A disabled slider submits nothing, a non-empty error blocks submit, and reset restores the initial value.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** thumb-contrast: The thumb and fill are visible against the track and the surface around it, so position is readable without the value text.
- **MUST** forced-colors: Keep the track outline, the fill, the thumb, and keyboard focus visible under forced colors.

## Accessibility

- Role: Slider
- Name: From the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the thumb. |
| Arrow Right / Arrow Up | Increase the value by one step. |
| Arrow Left / Arrow Down | Decrease the value by one step. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Increase or decrease by a tenth of the range. |
| Home / End | Move to min or max. |

## Rationale

- **One thumb, horizontal, with no tick marks.** The uses in the usage section need one value along the reading direction. A two-thumb range, a vertical slider, and tick marks can be added when a layout needs them.
- **The value text is the number in the reader's locale. There is no format parameter.** Units go in the label, such as "Volume (%)" or "Maximum price (USD)". A format parameter for units or currency can be added when several uses need the same one.
- **The value text is not editable.** A slider is for approximate values. When people need an exact number, use Text field, as the usage section says.
- **No required state.** A slider always has a value, so it can never be empty.
- **Disabled removes the thumb from keyboard navigation and greys every part.** Nothing can change while disabled, so focus would only be a stop with nothing to do. The value text stays readable so people still see the setting.
- **An error recolors the fill and thumb and always shows its message.** A value can be wrong for reasons outside the slider, such as a budget above an account limit. The message carries the meaning, so the danger color is never the only signal.
- **No selected, checked, or loading state.** A slider holds a number, not an on or off state. Work that follows a change belongs to the page, which can disable the slider while it waits.
- **One size, filling the width of its container.** The track length comes from the layout. The thumb is large enough to grab with a pointer. Sizes are spacing primitives because no semantic size role exists (tokens ADR 0003).
- **The label is visible and required. There is no label-free slider.** Position on a track does not say what it sets, for sighted people either.
- **The track runs in the reading direction, so it mirrors in right-to-left layouts.** Min sits at the start and max at the end. Arrow keys follow the visual direction.
- **Nothing animates. The thumb and fill move with the value.** Motion would lag behind the pointer while dragging.
- **In forced colors the track draws an outline, and the fill and thumb use a system color.** Forced colors drop background colors, which would leave an invisible track. An outlined track with a solid fill and thumb keeps the position visible.
- **The fill and thumb use the primary action color, not the brand color Progress bar uses.** A slider is a control, and action colors say it can be changed. Progress bar uses brand color because it cannot.
- **The disabled fill and thumb use the disabled border color.** No color token covers a disabled filled part. The disabled border color is visible against the disabled track and reads as unavailable, so a new token for one component is not needed.
- **The thumb border uses the surface color.** A ring in the surface color separates the thumb from the fill behind it, so the thumb edge stays visible where the two share a color.

## Links

### alternative

- [Progress bar](component.progress-bar) — Show progress or a measured amount people cannot change. A slider is a control. A bar that only reports a value must not look adjustable.
- [Select](component.select) — Choose from a few named options, such as Small, Medium, and Large. Named options are choices, not points on a scale. A select names each one.
- [Switch](component.switch) — Turn a single setting on or off. Two states are a toggle, not a range.
- [Text field](component.text-field) — Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.

### follows

- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Progress bar](component.progress-bar)
- [Select](component.select)
- [Text field](component.text-field)

## React implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/react-components`
- Component: `Slider`

### Import

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@taproot-ds/react-components";
```

### Usage

```tsx
<Slider
  label="Maximum price (USD)"
  hint="Shows homes at or below this price."
  name="max-price"
  min={0}
  max={2000}
  step={50}
  defaultValue={800}
  onChange={(price) => search({ maxPrice: price })}
/>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | prop | parameter `label` | string | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| `hint` | prop | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| `error` | prop | parameter `error` | string | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the slider invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| `value` | prop | parameter `value` | number | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. Defaults to min. |
| `defaultValue` | prop |  | `number` | The value at first when the parent does not control value. Form reset restores it. Defaults to min. |
| `min` | prop | parameter `min` | number | Smallest value, at the start of the track. |
| `max` | prop | parameter `max` | number | Largest value, at the end of the track. Greater than min. |
| `step` | prop | parameter `step` | number | Distance between the values people can choose, counted from min. The value is always min plus a whole number of steps. |
| `name` | prop | parameter `name` | string | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| `disabled` | prop | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Prevents changing the value. A disabled slider does not submit its value. |
| `onInput` | callback | event `input` |  | The value changed while a person drags the thumb or presses a key. Reported for every new value. |
| `onChange` | callback | event `change` |  | A person finished changing the value: released the thumb or the key. Reported once, and only when the value differs from the value before they started. |
| `className` | prop |  | `string` | Added to the root element's classes. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Value

Pass `value` with `onInput` to control the slider, or `defaultValue` to let it keep its own value.
A controlled slider shows only the `value` it is given, so a parent that wants the thumb to follow a
drag sets `value` in `onInput`. A value outside `min` and `max`, or between steps, shows as the
nearest allowed value; the prop itself is not rewritten.

### Input and change

`onInput` runs for every new value while a person drags or presses a key. `onChange` runs once when
they release, and only if the value differs from where they started
(`component.slider#change-on-release`). Run costly work, such as a new search, in `onChange`.
Neither runs for a new `value` prop or a form reset.

### Forms

With `name`, the value submits as a number string. A disabled slider submits nothing. A non-empty
`error` blocks the form from submitting, and the browser shows its text. Reset restores
`defaultValue` in an uncontrolled slider; a controlled slider keeps `value`.

### Value text

The value text is the number in the locale React Aria uses, which comes from an `I18nProvider` or
the browser. Put units in the label.

### Reading direction

The track follows the page's computed CSS `direction`: in a right-to-left page `min` is on the
right, and Arrow Right decreases the value. The value text keeps the reader's number format.

### Styles

```tsx
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/react-components/style.css";
```

content:
- component.accordion — Accordion: Use Accordion to let people expand only the sections of a long page they need, one heading at a time.
- component.alert — Alert: Use Alert for a short status message in the flow of the page, announced only when you ask.
- component.avatar — Avatar: Use Avatar to show a small picture of a person, so people can recognize who did, owns, or wrote something.
- component.badge — Badge: Use Badge for status or metadata. It is not a control.
- component.button — Button: Use Button to trigger an action or to submit or reset a form.
- component.card — Card: Use Card to present one subject as a bounded summary, such as an item in a collection, that a person can scan and act on.
- component.checkbox — Checkbox: Use Checkbox to turn one independent option on or off, with a label, hint, and error.
- component.dialog — Dialog: Use Dialog for a focused task or confirmation that temporarily blocks the surrounding view.
- component.divider — Divider: Use Divider to separate groups of related content within one surface or region with a thin line.
- component.icon — Icon: Use Icon to size and color a graphic you supply, beside text or inside another component.
- component.link — Link: Use Link to navigate to another page, a location on the page, or a resource.
- component.progress-bar — Progress bar: Use Progress bar to show how much of a task is done when you can measure it, such as an upload or a multi-step setup.
- component.radio-group — Radio group: Use Radio group to choose exactly one option from a short visible list.
- component.select — Select: Use Select to choose one value from a list with a label, hint, and error.
- component.spinner — Spinner: Use Spinner to show that something is loading or working when you cannot say how long it will take.
- component.switch — Switch: Use Switch to turn a setting on or off and apply the change immediately.
- component.tabs — Tabs: Use Tabs to switch between a few related views of the same subject, one view visible at a time.
- component.text-area — Text area: Use Text area to collect multiple lines of text with a label, hint, and error.
- component.text-field — Text field: Use Text field to collect a single line of text with a label, hint, and error.
- component.tooltip — Tooltip: Use Tooltip to show the name of an icon-only control when a person points at it or focuses it.

**No, Taproot doesn't have a slider web component yet, so there's no tag name to use.** The spec defines a Slider (`component.slider`), but React is its only implementation. Running `taproot get slider --impl web` returns "No web implementation for component.slider", and Slider isn't among the 20 components in `taproot list --impl web`.

I couldn't search the installed `web-components` package files directly because that command was denied, so this comes from the CLI only. I also wouldn't guess at a name like `<taproot-slider>`, since the guide says not to derive API names.

**What you can do instead:**
- **Use React:** if your project can use it, `Slider` from `@taproot-ds/react-components` is ready now.
- **Use a text field:** if people need an exact number, the spec recommends `component.text-field` over a slider anyway, and it has a web implementation.
